correctness.rationale: Exact product covariogram and normalized scale substitution yield (3); the gamma integral (4) proves (1) on an explicit positive small-radius interval. Fixed product e_d determines the monic root polynomial from precisely d−1 measured coefficients. Strictly positive simple-root perturbations prove their minimal number. Rouché multiset matching proves uniform 1/d Hölder on compact shape classes, with a product-normalized constant-term perturbation yielding optimality even near the cube. The standalone checker was run and passed; finite tests supplement an infinite-quantifier analytic proof.

Accessible own records were searched for recoverable claims (including planar pair-distance global moments). Primary Wang full HTML, and two highly relevant complete published research RESULTS, were compared on objects and implications. Residual risk from classical tables and inaccessible related free-path full text is identified; no exhaustive uniqueness is asserted.

value.rationale: The radial distance law is a highly compressed, orientation-free covariogram observable and generally fails to determine convex bodies. This work rigorously isolates an important natural subclass (all Euclidean orthotopes) where only d−1 local coefficients recover the complete scale-free side multiset, proves that no fewer coefficients suffice even generically, and identifies the sharp uniform quantitative loss at repeated roots. The sharp inverse and information count are meaningful beyond routine coefficient extraction; no broad reconstruction beyond orthotopes is asserted.
